iut_type: BLE product — RF PHY + SIG registration quote (System Design Co.)
customer_question: Internal quote preparation: what are the standard service fees for BLE RF PHY testing, proxy SIG registration, Compliance Folder creation, and Qualification Fee proxy payment?
question_variants: What is the standard fee for BLE RF PHY 2-item test?
How much does Allion charge for proxy SIG registration (Multi-Design)?
What is the cost breakdown for a BLE product registration with RF PHY test, proxy registration, Compliance Folder, and Qualification Fee?
actual_issue: Internal Allion thread for preparing a quote for System Design Co. The thread confirms standard pricing for the various service components in a BLE RF PHY + registration service package.
plain_english_explanation: Allion's quote for this BLE registration (as stated in this thread): BLE RF PHY test (2 items) = ¥200,000; proxy registration support (Multi-Design) = ¥250,000; Compliance Folder creation fee = ¥150,000; a second line also labeled Compliance Folder creation fee = ¥100,000; Qualification Fee = $12,000. The duplicate Compliance Folder line label appears as written in the source quote and is not explained elsewhere in the thread.
consultant_answer: Quote: RF PHY 2-item test ¥200,000; Multi-Design proxy registration support ¥250,000; Compliance Folder creation fee ¥150,000; Compliance Folder creation fee (second line) ¥100,000; Qualification Fee $12,000.
decision_logic: Standard pricing applies unless the project has exceptional scope or complexity. This registration is Multi-Design (referencing multiple QDIDs), which carries the ¥250,000 proxy registration support fee.
final_recommendation: Use these standard fees when preparing quotes. Confirm whether the registration is Single-Design or Multi-Design before issuing the quote.
risk_if_done_wrong: Issuing a Single-Design quote for a Multi-Design project leads to an underquote that must be corrected before or after order placement. Leaving an ambiguous duplicate line item (two 'Compliance Folder creation fee' entries) unexplained in a quote risks customer confusion or billing disputes.
